extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent applicants, patent agents, and patent office staff operating in GCC Member States (UAE, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar, Kuwait)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory rules governing patentable subject matter, application content and procedure, examination, rights and limitations, licensing (including compulsory licenses), fees, appeals, and administrative structure for patents under the Cooperation Council for the Arab States of the Gulf (GCC) Patent Regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention shall be patentable ... if it is new, involves an inventive step, industrially applicable and is not contrary to the laws of Islamic Shariya, or public order or to morality observed in the Cooperation Council States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to new products, industrial processes, or manufacturing methods. See detailed definitions of new, inventive step, and industrial applicability in Articles 2/2–2/4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of novelty / prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention is new if it is not anticipated by prior art. Prior art constituted by everything disclosed to the public anywhere by written or oral disclosure, by use, or by any other way before the relevant filing date or claimed priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public disclosure within one year before filing/priority may be disregarded if due to abusive actions against the applicant; disclosure at an officially recognized exhibition within six months preceding filing is not taken into account (Implementing Bylaws determine protection provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step (non-obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention involves an inventive step if, having regard to the relevant prior art, it would not have been obvious to a person having ordinary skill in the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention shall be considered industrially applicable if it can be produced or used in any type of industry, agriculture, fishing, or services. 'Industry' is interpreted broadly to include handicraft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public order, morality, and Shari'a exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions contrary to the laws of Islamic Shariya, public order, or morality observed in the Cooperation Council States are not patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ministerial Council may exclude inventions to safeguard public order or morality, including protection of human/animal/plant life & health or to avoid serious environmental damage (Article 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded subject matter (non-inventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following shall not be regarded as inventions: discoveries, scientific theories, mathematical methods, computer programs; schemes, rules, methods for business, purely mental acts, or games; plant varieties and species of animals, biological processes for producing plants or animals (except microbiological processes and their products); methods of surgical or therapeutic treatment or diagnostic methods applied to the human or animal body (except products used in these methods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation shall not protect varieties of plants or species of animals (Article 3/2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Security-related inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: If applications pertain to inventions connected with the security of any Cooperation Council State, procedures in the Implementing Bylaws shall apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-to-file rule for multiple applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If more than one application is filed for a particular invention, the patent shall be granted to the owner of the first application that has the earliest priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship and joint ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention is a result of joint efforts of several individuals, ownership of the patent shall belong to them equally, unless otherwise multilaterally agreed upon. A person is not an inventor if activities were limited to executing ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee inventions / employer rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Right to a patent shall be assigned to the employer if the invention resulted from execution of a contract or obligation to carry out inventive activities, or if the employer proves the invention would not have been achieved without use of employer facilities, means, or information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not prejudice the employee's right to special remuneration to be determined by a competent authority in the country where invention is made; agreements depriving employee of such rights void. Applies to government employees. An application filed by an employee within two years after termination of services is considered filed during employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file / representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent application shall be submitted to the Office by the inventor, his registered agent, or his successor in title, and accompanied by the prescribed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant is a non-GCC resident, he must appoint a registered GCC-resident agent to represent him before the Office (Article 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of application
rubrics_metrics.description: Application shall contain the title of the invention, a specification, one or more claims, one or more drawings (if any), and an abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification must disclose the invention sufficiently clearly and completely for a person skilled in the art to carry it out. Claims determine scope of protection; specification and drawings may be used to interpret claims. Claims must be clear, concise, and fully supported by the specification. Abstract serves only technical information and shall not be used to interpret the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single inventive concept requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall relate only to one invention, or to aspects so related as to constitute a single general inventive concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to application
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may introduce amendments he deems fit provided they do not constitute a substantive modification to the contents of the original application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claims and timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Application may contain claim of priority of a previous application filed in any State or regional office; application shall indicate date, filing number, and country of filing and produce proof, otherwise claim denied. Duration of priority is twelve Gregorian months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of application
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may withdraw his application at any time unless a final decision has been taken. Withdrawal does not entitle reclaiming documents or refund of fees or expenses incurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal and substantive examination procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the application satisfies terms, Office shall register the filing date and formally examine it. Substantive examination shall be carried out by the Office or referred to an approved examination authority after payment of Substantive Examination fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Formal Examination finds missing prescribed terms, Office may request completion within up to three months; failure causes lapse (Article 10). If Substantive Examination finds eligibility, Office grants patent, registers, and publishes it; if not eligible, Office rejects with reasons and publishes decision (Article 11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of formal defects timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Office may request applicant to complete formal requirements within three months from notification; failure to comply results in application lapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant, publication, and delivery of Letters Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: If Substantive Examination is satisfied, Office shall make a decision granting the patent, enter it in the register, and publish it. Letters Patent shall be delivered to owner three months from publication if no objection to Grievance Committee is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rejected, decision published and applicant informed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive rights conferred by patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent entitles owner to exploit the invention. For products: manufacturing, use, import, sale, offering for sale. For industrial processes: right to prevent others from actual use of the process and to prevent use/sale/import of products directly obtained by the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior good-faith user right
rubrics_metrics.description: An establishment that in good faith manufactures, uses an industrial manufacturing process, or makes serious preparations prior to the filing or priority date by another person shall have the right to continue such acts; assignment of that right to third parties only with whole business transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working requirement / exploitation obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner shall make sufficient exploitation of the patented invention in the Member States within three years from the date of grant. If grace period expires without sufficient exploitation, Article 19 provisions (compulsory licensing) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research and transit exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights under the patent shall not extend to acts carried out for scientific research purposes, or to use of patent articles on means of transportation temporarily or accidentally entering GCC territories (limited to necessities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term
rubrics_metrics.description: Term of a patent shall be twenty years counted from the date of filing the patent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual fees and grace periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent is subject to an annual fee paid in advance at the beginning of each year starting from the year following application filing date. Failure to pay within three months may be remedied within another three months with an additional fee; if unpaid within six months total, patent shall lapse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual fees may be paid in advance to cover validity term. Same provisions apply to applications. If Office delays decision >3 years, applicant may abstain from paying fees until grant and then pay unpaid annual fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractual license formalities and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner may license others to perform some or all exploitation acts; such license shall be in writing, signed, and authenticated in a GCC State. Licensing contract not effective vis-à-vis third parties unless entered in Office records and registration/fees paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractual license does not deprive owner from exploiting the patent or granting other licenses unless otherwise stated. Licensee cannot assign licensed rights unless expressly stipulated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office control over licensing contracts (competition/tech transfer concerns)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may request contracting parties to amend licensing contracts to rule out abuse of patent rights or negative influence on competition or technology dissemination; if parties fail to respond, Office may deny approval and refuse registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory license conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Board may grant compulsory license where owner never exploited or insufficiently exploited patent, observing: at least three years elapsed after grant; applicant proved efforts to obtain license from owner for adequate compensation under fair terms; license is not exclusive; license essentially granted to meet local market demands; license decision defines scope/terms; patent owner paid adequate compensation; exploitation limited to licensee and non-transferable except in certain ownership change with Board approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rule: for semiconductors, licensing permitted only for public, general, non-commercial purposes or to rectify anti-competitive practices by judicial/administrative decisions (Article 19/2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory license exceptions and emergency disregard
rubrics_metrics.description: Board may disregard the three-year and negotiation requirements if request due to state of emergency, dire public necessity, or for non-commercial use in one or more Council States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a government agency requests compulsory license on public interest grounds, Board may approve under Article 19 terms with observation of Article 20 clauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent invention / cross-licensing (patent dependence)
rubrics_metrics.description: If exploitation of an invention requires use of another invention and mutual agreement not reached, Board may grant compulsory license to one or both parties to exploit the other invention; Articles 19 and 20 observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory license cancellation grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Compulsory license shall be cancelled if: beneficiary fails to exploit sufficiently within two years (renewable for two more if legitimate reason); fails to pay due amounts within three months of maturity; fails to satisfy other terms stipulated; circumstances that led to grant end and unlikely to recur (while observing legitimate rights of licensee).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer, assignment, and inheritance of patent rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Ownership and all rights may be transferable by inheritance; ownership may be transferred wholly or partially with or without compensation. Requests to modify patent ownership or application particulars must be supported with evidence; transfers not effective against others until registration and publication of modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals and review of Office decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any decision issued by the Office may be appealed within three months from when it was known or published. Implementing Bylaws provide proceedings before the Committee and fees for appeal and renewal. Decisions of the Committee may be appealed before the competent authority in the host country; settlement made in conformity with this Regulation and host State laws or general rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction over infringement disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Competent authorities of each Member State shall examine disputes pertaining to infringement or imminent infringement and settle them pursuant to this Regulation and their own national patent regulations, if any, otherwise according to general rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent register and official gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall establish a register to enter patents and their particulars and shall publish an official gazette for all publications stipulated in the Regulation and Bylaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance Committee composition and decision rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee shall consist of twelve members (nationals of Member States) selected for personal capacity; each State nominates two members (one legally qualified, one technical specialist). Two legally qualified persons elected as chairman and vice-chairman for three-year session. Committee decisions by two-thirds majority of attendant members. Meetings held when at least one member from each State present; meeting may be postponed for two weeks if both members of any State cannot attend; if infeasibility persists next meeting is valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members must perform tasks neutrally and independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on Office/Committee staff and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the Committee, Board of Directors, and Patent Office staff may not, during employment or for two years following termination, submit patent applications on their behalf. Information in their possession is highly confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerated fees and fee prescription
rubrics_metrics.description: Office shall collect fees for specified instances (filing, granting and publication, annual fees, amendments, delay penalties, assignments, copies, compulsory license requests/grant, registration of license contracts, appeals, microorganism samples, temporary protection certificate during exhibition, patent search, substantive examination, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such fees shall be prescribed by the Implementing Bylaws (Article 30 lists 1–17).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to TRIPS exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: During the exclusion term, protection of products granted a patent by the Office shall not be valid in any Member State that is excluded in conformity with clause (4) of Article (65) of TRIPS annexed to the WTO agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementing Bylaws and governance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ministerial Council shall issue the Bylaws of this Regulation. Interpretation and proposals of modification are competency of the Financial and Economic Cooperation Committee following coordination with Scientific & Technical and Industrial Cooperation Committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation comes into force three months from publication and publication of Implementing Bylaws.
